sources.citation: Wikipedia (zh) 誒話 and Wikipedia (en) E language, accessed 2026-09-17 (secondary; phonology tables derived from Wei & Wei 2011 and Wang 2009).
sources.tag: read: notes on stress
sources.access_detail: read online, no copy kept
sources.note: zh: 7 citation tones (51, 31, 55, 35, 24; checked 54, 24), 'tone categories and values almost identical to Tuguai'; two-syllable sandhi resembles Zhuang and Tuguai. en: 7 tones. Neither says anything about stress.

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A. 1992. Fusion and diffusion in E, Guangxi Province, China. In Tom Dutton, Malcolm Ross & Darrell Tryon (eds), The language game: papers in memory of Donald C. Laycock, 135-144. Pacific Linguistics C-110. Canberra: ANU. (hdl 1885/145788; DOI 10.15144/PL-C110)
sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Whole chapter read (pp. 135-144): syllable = initial + final + tone; §3.2.1 'E tones' gives 8 tone categories with 5 contours (42, 21, 44, 323, 35, 55; tones 4/6/8 all 323, 7S/7L merged); §3.2.2 glottal-squeeze voice quality on low tones 2/4/6/8; fn. 3 'All the languages discussed here are, of course, tone languages.' No occurrence of stress/accent/prominence.
